free_tier.stated: A one-time free inference quota per model, 500K tokens per model, granted to new users on registration. It is calculated separately for each model and shared under the primary account, offsets pay-as-you-go online inference tokens only, and in Free Tokens Only mode the service is suspended near the quota so no fee accrues. The activity page states the quota does not expire but is subject to change

limits.value: 500K tokens per model, one-time; offsets online pay-as-you-go inference only, not batch inference, plugins, knowledge bases or context-cache storage

Model-list maximums per primary account (theoretical, subject to platform load; all endpoints of a base model share them), for the models the pricing page lists at 500k tokens: Seed 2.0 lite, mini, code-preview and pro 30K RPM and 1500K TPM; DeepSeek V4 pro and flash 260425 versions 15K RPM and 1500K TPM; DeepSeek V4 pro-ga and flash-ga 0.5K RPM and 1000K TPM; Seed 2.1 turbo 0.5K RPM and 1000K TPM (its free-quota row reads 500 tokens); retiring Seed 1.8 30K RPM and 1500K TPM, Seed 1.6 and Seed 1.6 flash 15K RPM and 800K TPM, DeepSeek V3.2 15K RPM and 1500K TPM. Skylark-pro has no row on the model list; which model version carries the quota is not stated

record.binding_note: the per-model 500K token quota is the only stated cap

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for email, username and password, or Google or GitHub sign-in. The quota page says to register and authenticate as a BytePlus user; the help centre says individual accounts reach a limited subset of products, business accounts need a business license and company details, and a valid credit card may be required to activate pay-as-you-go models; Free Tokens Only mode is open to identity-verified personal accounts and enterprise accounts; the campaign terms require enterprise information submission and judge uniqueness from email verification, ID documents, domain names, mobile numbers, devices and IP addresses. unverified: whether a card, phone number or identity verification is required before the quota is granted, which only an account shows

record.reliability_note: a separate Data Collaboration Rewards Campaign advertising 5M tokens daily per model behind real-name verification: the campaign page calls it an ongoing benefit while the activity page carries an earlier stated end date; daily resource pack distribution for 18 models, among them Seed 2.0 pro, lite and mini, Seed 1.6, 1.8, DeepSeek V3.2 and V4 pro and flash GA, ended on October 8, 2026
record.confidence_note: quota size and scope are documented; the identity requirement is unverified beyond the quoted terms

card.summary: Serverless microVM sandboxes that the vendor says start in under 150 ms, scale to tens of thousands created concurrently and to millions of vCPUs, support st...

free_tier.stated: Serverless microVM sandboxes that the vendor says start in under 150 ms, scale to tens of thousands created concurrently and to millions of vCPUs, support stateful long-running sandboxes, ship preconfigured templates, and bill at millisecond granularity with no charge while nothing is executing. Templates, large-scale image distribution, arbitrary specifications and MCP, API and SDK access are listed. No free tier is published.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: A microVM that bills only while executing is the right shape for evaluation fan-out, where a thousand short sandboxes each live a few seconds; it is the wrong shape for a service that must stay up, because the published selling point is that idle costs nothing precisely by not being a persistent host.

limits.value: The rate card and the signup gate are both behind an account: the public documentation renders as a script shell, so the only published numbers are third-party, and whether a personal account can create a sandbox at all was not established.

record.limits_note: The rate card and the signup gate are both behind an account: the public documentation renders as a script shell, so the only published numbers are third-party, and whether a personal account can create a sandbox at all was not established.
record.binding_note: The rate card and the signup gate are both behind an account: the public documentation renders as a script shell, so the only published numbers are third-party, and whether a personal account can create a sandbox at all was not established.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: no page stating the signup requirement was read; the record's evidence covers the sandbox mechanics (sub-150 ms starts, millisecond billing with no charge while idle, MCP/API/SDK access), a third-party rate of USD 0.0351 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0081 per GiB-hour, and a BytePlus billing page that returned only its navigation shell. Whether a personal account can create a sandbox at all was not established.

evidence.proved: 'sandboxes can start within 150ms and can be created concurrently at a scale of tens of thousands'; 'up to millions of vCPUs'; 'millisecond-level billing with no charges when not executing'; each sandbox is a microVM; MCP, API and SDK access
a third-party comparison lists USD 0.0351 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0081 per GiB-hour with no free tier, which is a claim about a third party and not a reading of BytePlus's own rate card
the billing overview page returns only its navigation shell with no rate table, so the vendor's own numbers could not be read

record.notes: Routes tried: the product solution page (read, product facts only), docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/faas/Billing_overview (navigation shell, no table), docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/faas/Overview_of_cloud_sandbox (same shell), and a broad search that returned only third-party comparison tables. Identity is left null rather than guessed: BytePlus sells to enterprises, and whether a personal account can top up without a company was not established. This is the one provider where the door is more likely to be the finding than the price.
